newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly slip with mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly slip with mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly lost ground Monday in quiet trade, pressured by forecasts this week for mild East Coast weather that should keep buyers relaxed, market sources said.
"It all comes down to weather, and if we don't get more hot weather soon, it could get messy," said one cash trader.
On average, low sulphurs on the East and Gulf Coasts came under the most pressure, with the prospect for lower utility burns, particularly with gas competitive, undermining sentiment.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent skidded 40 cents to about $16.25 a barrel on reports of a barge deal late Friday at $15.95 for 8/12 delivery.
NYH August one percent paper was done 25 cents lower at $16.20. September paper also was quoted a quarter weaker at $16, while Q3 was pegged at $16.65-85.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour slipped 15 cents to the $17.50 area.
High sulphurs in New York were down 10-25 cents, with 2.2 percent now talked at $15.00-25.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent was stable at $14.50-75, while one percent was a quarter lower at $15.50-75.

New York city gate swing gas prices inched up slightly Monday to about the $2.42/mmBtu level, or $15.25 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, eased modestly to about $2.20/mmBtu, or $13.86 a barrel.
